narrative:
The model estimates a 31% chance that you will fail your final year. That is not a certainty, but it is high enough under the school’s rule to require remedial courses as a precaution, since roughly one in three students with a comparable profile would be at risk.

The three most influential factors in this prediction all pushed toward passing. The strongest was your record of past class failures: you have none, which is a strong protective signal. Second was your intention to continue to higher education; it supports you and matches every passing student in the comparison group. Third was your mother’s work in services, a modest positive factor. Because the headline influences are protective, the remaining failure risk comes from smaller, combined circumstances rather than from those top items. Practically, your travel to school is over an hour, your weekly study time is under two hours, and you receive neither school nor family educational support, although you have no absences. To reduce the risk, build a regular study routine beyond two hours weekly, ask family or school staff for structured help, and manage travel fatigue. Your clean failure record and higher-education goal are strengths to build on.
